column1: # Lipid subclass -> membrane / curvature reference table.
# One row per subclass in MS2Lipid's vocabulary (63 positive-mode + 69 negative-mode
# classes, 97 distinct). This table is literature, not inference: every non-abstaining
# row names the citation that licenses it, and `citations.tsv` resolves the key.
# It replaces the three hard-coded dictionaries that used to live in membrane.py.
#               The LIPID MAPS category decides it (LIPIDMAPS2009): glycerophospholipid
#               is a membrane lipid, glycerolipid / sterol / fatty acyl / prenol is not.
#               Sphingolipids ABSTAIN rather than being assigned -- sphingomyelin is a
#               phospholipid and ceramide is not, so the category does not settle it.
#               E. coli makes neither, so this costs nothing here and stops the mapping
#               being wrong if it is ever reused on a eukaryotic dataset.
#               A property of the lipid, stated independently of `membrane`, so a
#               consumer can gate on membrane without this column having quietly
#               pre-gated itself. `not-applicable` means the species does not sit in a
#               bilayer at all (neutral core lipids, sterol esters, free fatty acyls).
#               `indeterminate` means the class is real but its shape is not settled --
# headgroup_group  PE/PC | PG | PS | PA/PI/neutral | NA
#               The four-way bucket the in-house mass-balance lane emits
#               (headgroup.py RESIDUE_GROUP). Present ONLY so MS2Lipid can be scored
#               against that lane at the resolution the lane can actually resolve.
#               It is a crosswalk for validation, not a call to make: MS2Lipid names
#               PE and PC separately and collapsing them throws that away.
#               Whether E. coli makes this class. Not used to gate any call -- it is the
#               instrument for measuring MS2Lipid's closed-world failure mode, which is
#               that handed a non-lipid (or a lipid outside its 97 classes) it still
#               returns one of the 97. A `no` call is not necessarily wrong, but a
#               *population* of `no` calls is a coverage claim that has to be discounted.

The dominant E. coli lipid and its non-bilayer component.
E. coli has no phosphatidylcholine synthase. A PC call here is either a real contaminant or a misprediction.
Transient intermediate of PE synthesis; decarboxylated fast, so present but not accumulated.
Measured spontaneous radius of curvature -46 A. Separable from PI only once a method names the subclass.
Not made by E. coli.
Cardiolipin. Measured-absent in this dataset (cl_bound.py), so a crop of CL calls is a red flag, not a discovery.
Dilyso-cardiolipin. Two chains on a cardiolipin head; geometry not measured.
Bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate. Grouped with PG by head chemistry, consistent with the prior lane.
Hemi-BMP, three chains on a glycerophosphoglycerol head. Two of the three blind controls are HBMP.
Phosphatidylethanol -- a transphosphatidylation artifact, not a biosynthetic product.
Phosphatidylmethanol -- as PEtOH.
Ether/plasmalogen PE. E. coli makes no ether lipids.
An oxidised chain is polar and turns back toward the interface; the headgroup no longer sets the shape.
As OxPE.
As OxPE.
As OxPE.
Measured +20 A -- the most positive spontaneous curvature of any membrane lipid reported.
N-acyl-lyso-PE. One O-acyl chain plus an N-acyl on the head; neither cone nor cylinder.
Glycerophospho-N-acyl-ethanolamine.
Diacylglycerol is a classic inverted-hexagonal-phase former. Not a membrane lipid by category, but it does force curvature where it partitions in.
Neutral core lipid; E. coli makes essentially none. A large TG/DG population in this dataset is a misprediction signature.
Monogalactosyldiacylglycerol -- the non-bilayer lipid of plants and cyanobacteria, absent from E. coli.
Sphingomyelin IS a phospholipid, but its category also holds ceramides, which are not. Abstain rather than assign.
Free sphingoid base -- single chain.
E. coli synthesises no bile acids. A bile-acid population in an E. coli extract is a misprediction signature.
Acylcarnitine -- E. coli has no carnitine acyltransferase pathway.
Ubiquinone. Genuinely present and abundant here -- the quinone signal is a documented part of this dataset.
